the entropy and complexity of EEG and intracranial signals tend to be highest when subjects are awake and aware and lowest in states with loss or impairment of awareness or consciousness (sleep stages, anesthesia, epileptic seizures).
the values of the complexity and entropy of the signals tend be greatest when the subject is in fully alert states and fall in states with loss or loss of consciousness.
the values of the entropy and complexity of neurophysiological signals tend to be highest in fully alert states and fall when the subjects are asleep, or in a coma or in epileptic seizures.

quantification of the structure of the brain activity in different states of consciousness.
the quantification of the complexity of the brain signals obtained from subjects in different states of consciousness.
the quantification and analysis of brain dynamics in different states of consciousness and the development of new methods for the study of cognition.
